market.fact: MarketsandMarkets: global fluoropolymers market USD 10.32bn in 2025, forecast USD 14.13bn by 2030 (6.5% CAGR). Asia Pacific is the largest region. Drivers cited: EVs (batteries, wiring, seals), semiconductors (ultra-pure grades), renewables (solar, Li-ion, hydrogen films/membranes). PTFE is the largest product type.

MarketsandMarkets: PTFE market USD 3.12bn in 2026, forecast USD 3.87bn by 2031 (4.4% CAGR). Asia Pacific held 50.5% share in 2025. Leading players named: Daikin, Dongyue, Gujarat Fluorochemicals. (Paid press release; publisher's own estimates.)

Global Market Insights: fluoropolymers used in semiconductor manufacturing were USD 1.6bn in 2025, forecast USD 3.1bn by 2035 (6.9% CAGR, 2026-35). Drivers: 300mm fab build-outs, EUV/high-NA lithography, advanced packaging. Top 5 hold ~63% (Chemours ~18.6%, Daikin, Syensqo, Arkema, Saint-Gobain).

Market-size estimates differ a lot by publisher (scope differs). Treat ~USD 9-10bn (2025) with ~4-6.5% CAGR as the range. Other pre-cutoff estimates are paywalled teasers; IMARC and Fortune pages were updated after the cutoff (see laterFacts).

Demand driver (AI/semis/new energy): Dongyue says H1 2026 fluoropolymer demand recovered and prices rose year on year because AI, semiconductors and new energy grew fast. Segment revenue +10.35%, segment result +69.2%.

Demand driver (data centres/semis): Chemours (Q4 2025 call) cited a strengthening semiconductor order book and rising AI/data-centre demand for high-purity PFA and Teflon products. It called auto, industrial and construction weak (down to flat).

Demand driver (data centres/semis), H1 2026 check: Chemours Q2 2026 says Performance Solutions sales rose 8% year on year on demand for specialty products for data centres and semiconductors. Overall APM sales still fell 6% because of the Capstone exit and the Washington Works outage.

Hydrogen is a weak spot, not a driver, in 2025: Chemours' FY2025 10-K cites 'weakness in ... products serving hydrogen markets' (Nafion membranes, Performance Solutions) as a reason for lower APM volumes. Chemours also announced closing its Villers-Saint-Paul (France) site, which was originally meant for hydrogen.

PFA (semiconductor-grade) context: PFA sells at a ~30-50% premium to PTFE. Foreign producers hold >70% of the global PFA market. In China only Dongyue and Juhua can make ultra-pure PFA in batches. SEMI certification takes 6-12 months plus 12-24 months of customer qualification. GFL is listed among the foreign PFA producers.

supplyExits.fact: 3M completed its exit from PFAS manufacturing at the end of 2025, per its annual report (quoted by ChemSec). Critics note 3M's sales of PFAS it made more than doubled in 2025 vs 2024 as it ran down output, and that ~14,000 3M products still contain PFAS bought from suppliers.
3M announced the exit on 20 Dec 2022, covering fluoropolymers (Dyneon), fluorinated fluids and PFAS-based additives, with a deadline of end-2025.

AGC Chemicals Europe proposed ceasing operations at its Hillhouse site (Thornton-Cleveleys, Lancashire, UK), which makes PTFE, ETFE and fluoroelastomers. Consultation of at least 45 days began 13 Jul 2026. If confirmed, production ends by end-2026. Affects ~190 employees and 18 agency staff. Reason given: four straight years of losses in a volatile, competitive market. Capacity in tonnes was not disclosed. No final decision found as of the cutoff.

AGC Hillhouse context: the site faces possible legal claims from residents over PFOA contamination (it emitted an estimated 49 t of PFOA from the 1950s to 2012). AGC did not cite this as a reason for closing.

Chemours restructuring: it completed the exit of the SPS Capstone product line in Q3 2025, announced the closure of its Villers-Saint-Paul (France) site, and continues a European asset review into 2027. No exit of fluoropolymer (PTFE/PFA) capacity was announced.

Chemours Washington Works (WV, main US fluoropolymer site): unscheduled full shutdown in 2025 (~USD 20m Q3 2025 hit), then another outage in Jan 2026 (est. USD 20-25m hit to Q1 2026 EBITDA). Q1 2026 APM Adjusted EBITDA was guided to breakeven to USD 5m. This is an involuntary supply disruption, not a permanent exit.

china.fact: Dongyue FY2025: fluoropolymer segment revenue RMB 3,930m (+2.75%), segment result RMB 357m (-29.8%), margin 9.07% (2024: 13.28%). Management: competition 'continued at the same intense level', average selling prices 'did not see significant improvement'. This is direct evidence of weak Chinese PTFE pricing in 2025.

Dongyue H1 2026: fluoropolymer revenue RMB 2,141m (+10.35% y/y), segment result RMB 439m (+69%), margin 20.49% (H1 2025: 13.36%). Product prices rose year on year. This shows Chinese fluoropolymer pricing turned up in 2026.

ChemNet (via ITA Beijing newsletter): from 1 Jun 2026 Chinese makers raised factory prices for all fluoropolymers, citing raw-material and logistics costs. PTFE and FEP +5%; battery-grade PVDF +5%; coating-grade PVDF +10%; fluororubber (FKM) up to +15% (or USD 1.38/kg).

LOW-CONFIDENCE: Chinese industry report says global PTFE capacity was ~320 kt in 2025, with China ~175 kt (55%). Dongyue ~60 kt, second only to Juhua. Sanmei's Shaowu base added 15 kt/yr (phase 1), online late 2025. China is still import-dependent in high-end grades (ePTFE, semiconductor grade). The same report has inconsistent refrigerant figures.

LOW-CONFIDENCE: same report: PVDF capacity China ~140 kt of ~230 kt global. Battery-grade PVDF averaged ~RMB 80,000-100,000/t in 2025 after peaking ~RMB 600,000/t in H1 2022. PVDF 'overcapacity persists 2026-2028'; 2024-26 outlook range RMB 70,000-120,000/t.

China 2026 HFC production quotas: total 797,845 t (+5,963 t vs 2025). R32 281,500 t (+1,171 t). R134a 211,500 t (+3,242 t). Quotas for HFC-143a, 227ea and 152a were cut. Supply stays capped (third-generation refrigerants).
China R32 price RMB 63,000/t (export RMB 61,000/t), R134a RMB 57,500/t, R125 RMB 46,000/t as of 12 Dec 2025 (Kaiyuan Securities). The 2026 quota plan keeps supply at roughly early-2025 levels.

China R32 RMB 63,000-63,500/t (a slight pullback from highs), R125 RMB 54,000-57,000/t, R134a RMB 58,500-59,000/t. Q2 2026 long-term contracts for R32/R410a were raised by RMB 3,000-5,000/t. Quota limits keep supply tight and inventories are low.

Dongyue H1 2026: refrigerant segment revenue RMB 2,569m (+12%), result RMB 1,246m (+21%), margin 48.5%. Higher R32 and R410a prices were 'mainly related to quota restrictions'. FY2025 refrigerant result was RMB 2,288m (+184%, margin 46.3%).

pfas.fact: ECHA's Risk Assessment Committee (RAC) adopted its final opinion on the universal PFAS restriction on 2 Mar 2026. SEAC agreed its draft opinion on 10 Mar 2026. Both were published on 26 Mar 2026 with a 60-day consultation on the SEAC draft (closed 25 May 2026). SEAC's final opinion is expected by end-2026, then the Commission drafts the restriction for a REACH Committee vote.

Fluoropolymers stay in scope. RAC backs a full restriction (option RO1) and rejects grouped derogations for so-called 'fully degradable PFAS' (fluoropolymers and volatile PFAS). SEAC agrees and calls the dossier's site-specific management plans for fluoropolymers/PFPEs impractical.

SEAC draft: general transition period of 18 months, plus use-specific derogations of 5 or 12 years where alternatives are lacking. It recommends an interim, time-limited generic derogation for 8 sectors added later that SEAC did not assess: printing, sealing, machinery, other medical, military, explosives, technical textiles, broader industrial uses.

RAC wants any derogation tied to site-specific PFAS management plans, emissions monitoring, supply-chain communication, consumer labelling and reporting of industrial emissions to ECHA. The restriction covers ~14,000 substances and their manufacture, placing on the market and use.

A European Parliament (ITRE) study on six key fluoropolymers and F-gases found substitution often not technically feasible in aerospace, defence, green energy and semiconductors. It recommended time-unlimited derogations for critical sectors and longer transitions for green technologies.

Risk read for exporters to Europe: as of the cutoff, no restriction is law. Earliest path is SEAC final (end-2026), then Commission draft, REACH Committee vote and Parliament/Council scrutiny, then 18 months before the general ban applies. Fluoropolymer sales to the EU therefore look exposed from roughly 2028 onward, except where use-specific 5/12-year derogations apply. This is an inference from the timeline above, not a sourced forecast.

usTrade.fact: Correction to the brief: there is no 2018 US order. In 2018 the US ITC made negative final injury determinations on PTFE resin from China and India: the India CVD case (Jul 2018) and the China/India AD cases (31 Oct 2018). So no orders were issued then.

The current US antidumping and countervailing duty orders on granular PTFE resin from India (and Russia) were published 15 Mar 2022 (87 FR 14509 / 14514). In the original investigation, GFL got an AD rate of 13.09% (10.01% after adjusting for export subsidies) and a CVD rate of 31.89%. US imports from India were USD 22.1m (2017), 31.1m (2018) and 12.0m (2019).
US AD administrative review (POR 1 Mar 2023 - 29 Feb 2024): final margin for GFL 1.83%, which became its cash deposit rate. All-others rate 10.36%.
Amended for ministerial errors: GFL AD margin 1.80% (same POR), effective 2 Apr 2026. This is GFL's current AD cash deposit rate.
US CVD administrative review (POR CY2023): final net countervailable subsidy rate for GFL (cross-owned with Inox Leasing and Finance) 5.16%.
Sunset review: the orders date from Mar 2022, so the first five-year sunset review falls due around Feb-Mar 2027. None had started or concluded by the cutoff, so there is no sunset outcome yet.

2025 US tariffs on India: 25% 'reciprocal' tariff effective 7 Aug 2025 (EO 14326), plus an extra 25% penalty for Russian-oil purchases effective 27 Aug 2025. Total 50% on most goods. Section 232 goods and Annex II items were excluded.

India-US deal: Trump announced on 2 Feb 2026 that tariffs on India would fall from 50% to 18%. A US-India joint statement on an interim framework followed on 6 Feb 2026, and the 25% Russia-oil penalty was removed by executive order. Plastics and rubber and organic chemicals were listed at 18%; generic pharma, gems and some others were set for zero. This was a framework, not a signed comprehensive BTA.

On 20 Feb 2026 the US Supreme Court ruled 6-3 that the IEEPA tariffs (reciprocal tariffs and the India penalty) were unlawful. The administration replaced them with a temporary Section 122 global tariff of 10% from 24 Feb 2026, limited to 150 days. India's rate fell from 18% to 10%.

The Section 122 surcharge lapsed on 24 Jul 2026. Under USTR's 23 Jul notice, India is among 17 economies facing a 10% Section 301 forced-labour duty, which can last up to 4 years. Chemicals are not exempt; pharmaceuticals and semiconductors are zero. The India-US trade deal was still not concluded.

On 11 Mar 2026 USTR started a Section 301 investigation into 'structural excess capacity' in 16 economies, including India (sectors flagged for India: solar modules, textiles, health). It was pending at the cutoff and could lead to more tariffs on industrial goods.

R125 angle: the US has AD duties on R-125 (pentafluoroethane) from China. Final results of the administrative review (POR Mar 2023 - Feb 2024): Zhejiang Sanmei 48.67%, China-wide entity 267.51%. This shuts most Chinese R125 out of the US and helps non-Chinese suppliers. No US trade action specific to Indian R125 was found.

hfc.fact: MoEFCC Office Memorandum (1 Apr 2026). India's HFC baseline = average HFC production/consumption in 2024, 2025 and 2026 plus 65% of the 2009-10 HCFC-22 baseline. Freeze from 1 Jan 2028. Reductions: 10% by 2032, 20% by 2037, 30% by 2042, 85% by 2047. The baseline will be set as of 1 Jan 2027, and the ODS Rules 2000 will be amended.

The same OM says no environmental clearance will be granted for new or added HFC capacity (controlled uses) beyond 31 Dec 2027. Capacity already cleared cannot start production after 31 Dec 2027. Future production permits will consider the capacity of units operating as on 1 Jan 2028. Feedstock uses are exempt. HFCs made in India: HFC-32, HFC-134a, HFC-125. This explains the 2026-27 rush to commission R32/R134a capacity.

Quota allocation: no HFC quota rules or company quotas had been notified by the cutoff. SRF (Q4 FY26 call) flagged uncertainty over how the government will treat HCFC inclusion and quota allocation. It called CY2027 a 'free year', with quota constraints from 1 Jan 2028.
UNEP: India is in Kigali Group 2 (with Gulf states, Iran, Iraq, Pakistan). Group 2's freeze is 2028, four years after Group 1's 2024 freeze.
The Union Cabinet approved ratifying the Kigali Amendment on 18 Aug 2021, with a national HFC phase-down strategy to follow.
HCFC phase-out: India met the 67.5% HCFC phase-out target (production and consumption for controlled uses) as of 1 Jan 2025.

HCFC phase-out: Stage III of India's HCFC Phase-out Management Plan aims for complete phase-out by 2030 (97.5% cut, with a 2.5% servicing tail allowed to 2040 per Montreal Protocol rules). HCFC-22 used as feedstock (e.g. for PTFE/TFE) is not controlled.

R32 price trend 2026 (China benchmark, which drives import parity): about RMB 63,000/t in Dec 2025 and RMB 63,000-63,500/t in Apr 2026. Prices are near multi-year highs, held up by capped Chinese quotas and higher quarterly contract prices. See the china section for sources.
Navin Fluorine board approved INR 236.5 crore of capex for up to 15,000 MTPA of additional HFC (R32) capacity, funded from internal accruals.

SRF: about INR 88 crore Dahej HFC debottleneck, taking HFC capacity above 65,000 MTPA, in line with its Kigali entitlement. Separately, the Odisha HFO project's capex was raised to ~INR 2,300 crore: 20,000 MTPA HFO (1234yf/ze, 1233zd) plus 30,000 MTPA HF, targeted around Feb 2028.

GFL plans to add R134a capacity alongside its R32, R22, R125 and R410A to fully use its Kigali entitlement. It says it already has approvals and infrastructure; tonnage and capex were not disclosed. It also set up a semiconductor and advanced-materials subsidiary (GFCL Semiconductor and Advanced Materials Ltd, incorporated 26 Jun 2026).
GFL R32 expansion: per a search summary of the Q1 FY27 call, the CEO said it would be commissioned in Q2 FY27 (Jul-Sep 2026), and R134a within FY27. Not checked line by line against the transcript.

battery.fact: India PLI-ACC: INR 18,100 crore, 50 GWh target. 40 GWh was allocated in earlier rounds. The Ministry of Heavy Industries tendered the last 10 GWh for grid-scale storage (bids due 13 Oct 2026). Bidders must reach 25% domestic value addition within 2 years and 40% within 5, and commit to 1-4 GWh each.

Battery-components policy: India was reported (citing Bloomberg) to be preparing an incentive of up to INR 13,000 crore (~USD 1.37bn) for anode and cathode active materials, electrolytes, separator film and copper foil. It was heading to the Finance Ministry's Expenditure Finance Committee and was not approved by the cutoff. The ministry said on 10 Feb that PLI cell makers' delays stemmed partly from 'non-availability of upstream components'.

India demand outlook (Nuvama): advanced-chemistry-cell demand to grow at a 39% CAGR over 2025-30, BESS demand at a 78% CAGR, and EV battery demand ~35% CAGR over FY25-30. More than 10 makers have announced ~178 GWh of battery capacity.

NITI Aayog estimates India's annual battery demand at ~250 GWh by 2030 (~40% from EVs). In 2024 the Heavy Industries Secretary expected 110-120 GWh of cell capacity by 2027-28 (50 GWh under PLI plus 60-70 GWh from others).
India BESS: 8.2 GWh installed in 1H 2026 (~84x 1H 2025), 9.3 GWh cumulative by end-Jun 2026. Storage tenders were 28 GW in 1H 2026, with ~9 GW auctioned.

On 15 Jul 2025, China's MOFCOM and MOST added battery cathode preparation technology (LFP, LMFP, phosphate precursors) and five lithium extraction/processing technologies to the catalogue of technologies restricted from export. Licences are now needed to transfer them abroad.

On 9 Oct 2025, China's Announcement No. 58 put export controls on lithium batteries, cathode materials, artificial graphite anode and related equipment/technology, effective 8 Nov 2025. On 7 Nov 2025, Announcement No. 70 suspended it until 10 Nov 2026. The July 2025 technology-export restrictions were not part of that suspension.

LiPF6 price (China): ~RMB 47,000/t in Jul 2025, rising to ~RMB 180,000/t by end-Dec 2025 (+280%), then ~RMB 138,000/t on 3 Feb 2026 (-20%+ in a month). An industry deficit of ~7,000 t was projected for Q4 2026.

LiPF6 battery-grade spot RMB 105,000-120,000/t on 21 May 2026, with high-end grades at RMB 170,000-180,000/t. Effective capacity is only ~270-300 kt of 500 kt nominal; social inventory ~6,000 t (about a week). Cost of production is ~RMB 85,000-90,000/t, with lithium carbonate at RMB 192,000/t.

indiaTrade.fact: DGTR final findings (19 Sep 2025) recommended AD duty on PTFE from China and Russia. Applicant: GFL. POI Apr 2023 - Mar 2024. China: Shandong Dongyue USD 2,884.01/MT; Shaowu Yonghe Jintang USD 5,206.75/MT; Chemours Changshu and Zhonghao Chenguang nil (negative margins); others USD 5,933.70/MT. Russia: any producer USD 4,578.80/MT.

DGTR opened a fresh AD investigation on PTFE from China and Russia (F. No. 6/07/2026-DGTR) on 20 Mar 2026. Applicant GFL, supporter SRF. POI 1 Oct 2024 - 30 Sep 2025. No Finance Ministry notification imposing the Sep-2025 recommendation was found, which suggests it was not imposed (inference, not confirmed).

FKM (fluoroelastomer) from China: the second sunset review was opened on GFL's application (16 Jun 2025), and the existing duty was extended to 26 Feb 2026 (Notification 29/2025-Customs (ADD), 19 Aug 2025). DGTR final findings of 29 Oct 2025 recommended continuing the duty for 5 years at USD 1.04-8.86/kg.

R-125 (HFC-125) from China: DGTR final findings (Case AD(OI)-31/2025, dated 23 Sep 2026) recommended AD duty of USD 1,335/MT. Joint applicants SRF and GFL, who make 100% of domestic output. Imposition was not confirmed by the cutoff.
India imposed a five-year AD duty of up to USD 5,251/t on R-134a from China (finance ministry notification, Dec 2025), on DGTR's recommendation.

ICRA (chlor-alkali): caustic soda prices eased ~2-4% in FY2026, partly offset by a West Asia-driven spike in Mar 2026. ECU realisations rose 2% y/y in FY2026. Over 11M FY2026, imports fell ~52% and exports rose 27%. Sector outlook negative because of oversupply, energy costs and negative chlorine realisations.
Indian caustic soda prices rose ~15-20% y/y in Mar-Apr 2026 on war-linked energy costs. Power is 30-40% of production cost (CRISIL).
Grasim Q3 FY26 (Oct-Dec 2025): caustic CFR-SEA USD 443/t (-14% y/y, a two-year low); ECU INR 32,079/t (-6% y/y), dragged down by negative chlorine realisations.
Grasim Q1 FY27 (Apr-Jun 2026): caustic CFR-SEA USD 483/t (+3% y/y, second straight quarterly recovery); ECU INR 37,955/t (+6% y/y). Chlorine realisations got worse.

critiques.argument: Valuation full: 53x FY28E EPS vs its 52x target; battery chemicals may take longer to contribute (only LiPF6 meaningful in FY27)
Premium valuation: P/E ~89 vs 3-yr average 59 and 5-yr average 36
Valuations leave limited cushion despite fluoropolymer growth (SELL TP 3,373); stays negative after Q1 at TP 4,612
Battery-chemicals customer approvals could take longer amid industry uncertainty; ramp-up delay is the key downside to FY28E when full utilisation is targeted

EV business still loss-making: Q1FY27 battery revenue Rs 290 mn with EBITDA loss Rs 300 mn (Q4FY26: Rs 110 mn revenue, Rs 450 mn EBITDA loss); FY27 is a transition year and full potential only in FY29

Big gap between guidance and run-rate: GFCL EV FY27 revenue guided Rs 5-7bn with EBITDA break-even, yet Q1 battery revenue was Rs 290 mn and management targets only a three-digit (Rs 100 cr+) quarterly run-rate by Q4FY27
critiques.who: IDBI Capital visit note vs PL/ICICI Direct Q1 notes (our comparison)

critiques.argument: Capex and leverage: FY27 capex ~Rs 3,100 cr (Rs 2,300 cr battery + Rs 800 cr chemicals), Rs 6,000 cr cumulative battery capex by FY28; ICICI Direct sees debt/equity rising from 0.3x (FY26) to 0.6x (FY27E-28E)
Oman battery project on hold (geopolitics, delays); Oman-specific sovereign funding will not move to India, so new funding is needed
Chinese competition, heavy Rs 6,000 cr capex, departure of key executives, and valuation far above peers; any battery delay or fluoropolymer downturn could de-rate the stock
Brokers flagged heightened competition, lower realisations and expansion execution risk; Emkay blamed the Q4 loss on overheads and slow revenue ramp-up in battery materials
HFC pricing pressure and delayed offtake in fluoropolymers and battery materials are the main risks
Counterpoint on China: management sees limited direct Chinese competition in the high-value fluoropolymer grades it targets
